narrative.overview: The site behaves like the front door of a parish: before anything else it tells a stranger where, when and who. The seal's deep indigo is used as large committed fields against an indigo-tinted off-white, and real photographs of the congregation carry the warmth.
keyCharacteristics: Seal indigo as a field color, not a sprinkle of accent.
Hairline dividers and lists in place of cards.
Pill buttons; photographs and panels with modest radii.
Phone numbers, addresses and times are always tappable and near the top.

rules.name: The Seal-Only Rule
rules.body: Brand color is the logo's indigo and its tints. Do not introduce a second hue for emphasis.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: Light grounds are indigo-tinted whites; warm cream is out.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: Headings use Young Serif (one weight, never bolded); everything read or tapped uses Figtree.

rules.name: The Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are indigo-tinted, soft, negative-spread; never grey or hard-offset.

dos: Do keep service time, address and phone within the first screen.
Do use only content that exists in the parish's own materials.
Do make every phone, email and address tappable.
donts: Don't add a second brand hue, cream grounds, or gradient text.
Don't use three-equal-card icon rows, centered hero stacks, or nested cards.
Don't invent testimonials, statistics, sermons or events.
Don't use grey or hard-offset shadows.
